Apollo 8 Mission Notes

Apollo 8 was launched on December 21, 1968, and was the first crewed spacecraft to travel to the Moon and orbit it. The crew consisted of Frank Borman, James Lovell, and William Anders. During the mission, the astronauts completed ten lunar orbits and photographed the lunar surface. Apollo 8 was an important step toward achieving a crewed Moon landing during the Apollo program.

Apollo 14 Mission Notes

Apollo 14 launched on January 31, 1971, with astronauts Alan Shepard, Edgar Mitchell, and Stuart Roosa aboard. It was the third successful crewed lunar landing mission. Shepard and Mitchell explored the lunar surface in the Fra Mauro region, collected geological samples, and conducted scientific experiments. The mission returned valuable information about the Moon's geology.

It was a wonderful mission.

Apollo 13 Mission Notes

Apollo 13 launched on April 11, 1970, with astronauts James Lovell, John Swigert, and Fred Haise. An oxygen tank explosion damaged the spacecraft during its journey to the Moon, forcing NASA to abandon the planned lunar landing. The crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat while mission control worked to bring them safely home. Apollo 13 successfully returned to Earth on April 17, 1970. The mission became famous for its emergency response and engineering problem-solving.

Apollo 7 Mission Notes

Apollo 7 launched on October 11, 1968, with astronauts Walter Schirra, Donn Eisele, and Walter Cunningham. It was the first crewed mission of the Apollo program and the first crewed flight of the Apollo command and service module. The mission lasted approximately eleven days and tested important spacecraft systems in Earth orbit. Apollo 7 helped establish the technical foundation for the later crewed lunar missions.
